about: Libraries common in 32-bit DOS and Win32 games of about 1993-2010: how to recognise them in a game (strings in the executable, imported DLLs, files next to it), what the kit can do for them and what to know when reading or porting the code. Evidence: 'strings' are byte strings searched in the executable (case-sensitive, one hit is enough), 'version' a regular expression whose group 1 is the version, 'imports' DLL names (PE), 'import_prefix' imported function name prefixes, 'files' file name patterns searched in the game directory (case-insensitive), 'magic' the first bytes of data files there. Prototypes and signatures name the kit's files.

libraries.name: Watcom C/C++ run-time library
libraries.license: proprietary (Open Watcom: Sybase Open Watcom Public License)
libraries.version: WATCOM C/C\+\+(?:32|16)? Run-Time system\. \(c\) Copyright by WATCOM International Corp\. 1988-(\d{4})
libraries.notes: Statically linked into every Watcom program. The copyright year in the run-time banner dates the compiler (1994: 10.0, 1995: 10.5, 1996: 10.6, 1997-1998: 11.0). Shipped signatures are Open Watcom 1.9/2.0; build your own from an original compiler with 'retrokit sigs build'. Register convention: arguments in EAX, EDX, EBX, ECX; variadic functions take them on the stack.

libraries.name: Miles Sound System / Audio Interface Library (AIL)
libraries.vendor: Miles Design, later RAD Game Tools
libraries.license: proprietary (AIL 2.0 for 16-bit DOS was put in the public domain)
libraries.notes: Digital audio and MIDI through loadable drivers (.DIG digital, .MDI MIDI; the setup program writes DIG.INI / MDI.INI). Music is usually Extended MIDI (XMIDI, .XMI: IFF 'FORM XDIR'/'XMID' with per-sequence timbre lists); convert it to standard MIDI for a port. Win32 versions export AIL_* functions by name from MSS32.DLL, which names the call sites directly. Statically linked DOS builds need learned signatures ('retrokit sigs learn'). Port: an audio mixer (SDL_mixer, miniaudio) plus an XMIDI-to-MIDI converter and a General MIDI synthesizer.

libraries.name: HMI Sound Operating System (SOS)
libraries.notes: Sound and music library of many mid-1990s DOS games; drivers in HMIDRV.386 / HMIMDRV.386, music in HMI's MIDI variants (.HMP, .HMI), which convert to standard MIDI. Port: audio mixer plus HMP-to-MIDI conversion.

libraries.name: DIGPAK / MIDPAK
libraries.vendor: The Audio Solution (John W. Ratcliff), drivers by John Miles
libraries.notes: TSR sound drivers loaded before the game and called through a software interrupt (DIGPAK: INT 66h) rather than linked code. MIDPAK plays XMIDI.

libraries.name: DiamondWare Sound ToolKit
libraries.notes: Digitized sound and music mixing toolkit for DOS and Windows.

libraries.name: Smacker video
libraries.notes: 8-bit palettised video (.SMK, signature 'SMK2'/'SMK4'). The Win32 API is exported by name from SMACKW32.DLL (SmackOpen, SmackDoFrame, SmackNextFrame, SmackWait, SmackToBuffer, SmackClose); DOS games link it statically. Port: FFmpeg or libsmacker decode .SMK; 'retrokit flic' covers the older Autodesk FLI/FLC instead.

libraries.name: Bink video
libraries.notes: Video codec from 1999 on (.BIK, signature 'BIK'). API exported by name from BINKW32.DLL (BinkOpen, BinkDoFrame, BinkNextFrame, BinkWait, BinkCopyToBuffer, BinkClose). Port: FFmpeg decodes Bink 1.

libraries.name: Granny 3D
libraries.notes: 3D model and animation runtime (.gr2 files). API exported by name.

libraries.name: FMOD
libraries.notes: Sound library (FMOD 3: FSOUND_*/FMUSIC_* functions, FMOD Ex from 2004: C++ classes). Imports name the call sites.

libraries.name: BASS
libraries.notes: Sound library; BASS_* functions imported by name.

libraries.name: DirectX
libraries.notes: COM interfaces: after the Create call every use is an indirect call through a vtable ([reg+offset]); naming them needs the interface layouts (roadmap step 9). DirectDraw (DDRAW) and DirectSound are the usual pair for 2D games.

libraries.name: zlib
libraries.notes: Deflate compression for archives and save games; the version string is usually linked in. Shipped signatures: 1.0.4, 1.1.3, 1.1.4, 1.2.3 compiled with Open Watcom (DOS); MSVC builds need learned or locally built signatures. Port: link zlib itself.

libraries.name: IJG libjpeg
libraries.notes: JPEG decoding/encoding; the error message table is linked in. Shipped signatures: 6b compiled with Open Watcom. Port: libjpeg(-turbo).

libraries.name: libpng
libraries.notes: PNG images; usually together with zlib.

libraries.name: PKWARE Data Compression Library (implode/explode)
libraries.notes: Implode/explode compression of game archives. Port: zlib's contrib/blast decompresses the format.

libraries.name: Lua
libraries.notes: Scripting language; game logic may live in .lua or precompiled chunks (signature ESC 'Lua').

libraries.name: Ogg Vorbis
libraries.notes: Compressed audio from about 2001 on.

libraries.name: Allegro
libraries.notes: Game programming library; the DOS version is mostly built with DJGPP (COFF/go32, not LE), the Win32 one with MSVC or MinGW.

libraries.name: VESA BIOS Extensions / UniVBE
libraries.notes: SVGA graphics through INT 10h AX=4Fxxh; a linear frame buffer is mapped with DPMI. SciTech MGL games link SciTech's library.

libraries.name: Rob Northen Compression (ProPack)
libraries.notes: Packed data files start with 'RNC' + method byte; 'retrokit rnc' unpacks method 1.
